about: The answers candidate's cast and trigger rules with the attack left to Forge (no attack policy), for a side-by-side run on the same tables. Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: The answers candidate: version 2 (acorns) with its attack, its two trigger rules and its holds unchanged, answer rules added in front of the engine and the engine list reordered so that the cards no rule named are no longer starved. Written from the 200 tables of bots of ab-run #27 (seed 20261260), where acorns won 47 and the stock pilot of the same deck 46: the engine rules bought 1.35 goldfish turns and nothing at the table. Why: the first play or activate rule with something to do acts, and version 2's 36-card engine list nearly always had something, so cards it did not name were left to Forge only on turns when every rule was idle. Of the games each was drawn, stock cast against acorns: Skyfisher Spider 45/50 against 22/60, Casualties of War 39/45 against 17/48, Poison-Tip Archer 40/55 against 16/56, Rootcast Apprenticeship 41/54 against 21/59, Swarmyard Massacre 45/46 against 28/45, Binding the Old Gods 27/56 against 9/51; in hand at a loss 23, 24, 24, 29, 18 and 23 times under acorns. Decree of Pain (AI:RemoveDeck:All) was cast in none of 108 games and in hand at 35 of acorns' 151 losses; on the own turns it sat there castable by land count the largest opposing board was nine creatures against our five (medians), at 16 life. Rule numbers below are this file's. Rules 3-4, Decree of Pain (destroys every creature, draws one a creature): when an opponent could kill us next turn with more power than ours (threat >= life, opp_power > power), or an opponent has eight creatures or more, more than we have, and more power. Not the wipe of a deck that is ahead. Rule 5, Swarmyard Massacre (two Squirrels, then -X/-X to every creature that is not an Insect, Rat, Spider or Squirrel, X our count of those) as soon as an opponent has three creatures: it is nearly one-sided here, and stock cast it with eight opposing creatures (median). Taken out of the engine list, where it was cast for two Squirrels into an empty board. Rule 6, Casualties of War with any opposing creature, unless our Garruk is out (its modes are chosen by Forge's AI as the spell is cast, and the planeswalker mode must not find ours). Local casts: four targets each time, all opponents'. Rules 7-8, Binding the Old Gods, and Skyfisher Spider with a token to give up, ahead of the engine when an opponent has more power than we have (Forge chooses the target of chapter I and of the Spider's trigger). Locally Binding's chapter I took an opposing commander or best creature all five times (Galadriel twice, Demon of Fate's Design, Sporemound, Great Oak Guardian); the Spider was cast twice by the first form of this rule, which counted any creature, with no token to give, and Forge declined the trigger both times (it would have had to sacrifice Hazel or a nontoken creature): hence the token condition. Rules 9-10, End-Raze Forerunners: the base's main-phase-one play and hold, at three ready attackers instead of four (it sat in hand at 11 of acorns' losses against 5 of stock's; with three ready attackers +2/+2, vigilance and trample on them is still the best use of eight mana). Rule 11, the engine list reordered: Beledros Witherbloom and Garruk first (castable only with six or seven mana, and then the best use of it: the first castable card of the list is taken, so a cheap card ahead of them used to eat the turn), then the base's engine order, with Skyfisher Spider, Poison-Tip Archer (a second Zulaport with deathtouch and reach) and Binding the Old Gods after Beastmaster Ascension; Hazel's Brewmaster and Arasta moved up behind the drain and draw pieces; Rootcast Apprenticeship added (Forge picks its modes and targets as it is cast: locally two +1/+1 counter modes on Hazel and copies of Squirrel tokens); Woe Strider and Insatiable Frugivore left near the end where the base had them. Rule 19, Plaguecrafter with a token to give up; rule 20, Cache Grab in the second main phase ahead of the mana sinks of rules 21-25 (stock cast it 48/63, acorns 36/59). Trigger rule 3: Skyfisher Spider's 'sacrifice another creature' with a token to give: Forge sacrifices its lowest-rated creature and aims the destroy; in the exam its trigger destroyed something on 13 of stock's 47 casts and 12 of acorns' 23. Left to Forge as before, and cast by it: Putrefy, Saw in Half, Tear Asunder, Windgrace's Judgment, Haywire Mite, Chittering Witch's and Garruk's abilities. Out of reach: Maelstrom Pulse, scripted as a Pump spell, which Forge's AI never casts (0 of 96 games drawn in the exam, both pilots) and a rule can cast only through Forge's own logic since it needs a target; Decree of Pain's cycling (an ability in hand). Checked at 16 local tables of bots (seeds 20263130 and 20263131; the Spider's token condition of rule 8 was added after them and has not been played).
